headline: Jefferies strategist Chris Wood says strong AI-driven company profits have so far shielded US stocks from rising bond yields, but the bond market is becoming a growing risk.
score_reason: Kept at 5: one strategist's opinion rather than a new event, though the yield figures are notable.
importance_line: It matters to savers and pension holders whose funds hold US stocks and bonds because US government bond yields are at their highest since 2002, but it is one analyst's view of risks, not a forecast that has come true.
summary: The Economic Times reports that Chris Wood, a strategist at the investment bank Jefferies, says in his newsletter that profits boosted by AI spending have helped US stocks shrug off rising bond yields, with US 10-year and 30-year yields at 5.34% and 5.69%, the highest since 2002. His three worries are whether AI spending will earn enough to justify its cost, a long-running fall in rich-country government bond prices, and shifting world politics.
